Figure_16_Second_order_obstruction.caption: Figure 16. An infinitesimal flex need not be a realizable constrained motion. A, A planar labelled K4 framework with all six pair distances fixed. Blue arrow moves vertex 4 out of plane. Teal/orange edges carry positive/negative stress coefficients; this is a mathematical fixture, not a chemical molecule. B, The rank-one stress matrix with u=(1,-1,-1,1); off-diagonal entries are minus the edge stresses. C, The proposed straight displacement changes the three incident distances quadratically, although every first derivative is zero. D, Symbolic rational arithmetic gives rank R=5, Rv=0, R-transpose omega=0 and omega-transpose b(v)=1. Thus Ra+b(v)=0 has no solution. The actual full-distance shape quotient is a singleton. A first-order kernel therefore overstates realizable flexibility at this singular point.

Figure_17_Realizable_sensitivity.caption: Figure 17. Realizable torsional sensitivity on the biological cohort. A, The first archived conformer of isomer A in the previously selected 81dbd5f36b7abada case; coloured segments 1 and 2 mark the first two eligible root-oriented bridge bonds (S–N and S–aryl), with wire shells at their endpoints. These are kinematic rotations and may have large energetic barriers. B, Persistent response rank on all 206 first conformers from 103 parents, using a heavy-atom mass-orthonormal torsion basis, fixed baseline response normalization, relative tolerance 10^-8 and absolute floor 10^-12. Multiplicities share a marker. Two isomers have k=20 and ranks 16 and 17; the other 204 have rank k. C, Cumulative smallest-to-largest singular-value ratios; two k>18 cases have s_k=0 by dimension and are omitted from the log axis, so curves terminate at 204/206. All three representations retain 204 full-rank cases at relative tolerances 10^-6,10^-8,10^-10. D, Eigenvalues of the first fixed normalized response coordinate: ordinary chart second derivative versus the Levi-Civita Hessian, expressed in the same all-atom mass-orthonormal basis of the two-coordinate case family. These local derivatives hold inside the archived filtration chamber; they do not predict activity.

Figure_18_Periodic_energy_domains.caption: Figure 18. One two-coordinate molecular case, with its periodic parameter topology made explicit. A,B, The same square grids wrapped onto an illustrative torus; the torus is the angle domain and is not a molecular surface. C,D, Unwrapped 65-by65 energy samples for the first archived conformer of each of the two stereoisomers. Opposite edges identify. The energy is evaluated with MMFF94s after hydrogen-only optimization at the base, followed by exact bridge rotations without further minimization. Each isomer uses its own E(0,0) baseline shared with its 33-by33 grid. Colour displays 1+DeltaE/(1 kcal/mol) on a common logarithmic scale; white contours are DeltaE=1, 5, 20 kcal/mol and orange marks the base. Small negative roundoff at the baseline is clipped only for logarithmic display. All raw energies, including severe high-energy clashes, are archived. The different independently generated base conformers are not an exact mirror control, and differences between these restricted surfaces are not an enantiomer free-energy difference.

Figure_19_Persistence_and_measure.caption: Figure 19. Periodic sublevel persistence and measure sensitivity on the same frozen case. A,B, Every H1 interval in the periodic vertex cubical energy filtration over F2, shown separately at 33 and 65 samples per angle. Arrowed bars are essential, with births near 5 and 16 kcal/mol; horizontal coordinates are 1+DeltaE/(1 kcal/mol) on a log axis. Both terminal complexes have Betti numbers (1,2,1), forced by the toroidal parameter domain. C, Odd-kernel mean squared norms at sigma=1 under uniform angle, Boltzmann angle, and Boltzmann-times-metric-volume weights at 298.15 K. One shared fine-grid uniform RMS normalizes both isomers for all weight rules. The metric-volume rule belongs to an explicitly defined reduced quotient kinetic model, not the full molecular canonical distribution. Coarse/fine markers nearly coincide; this is finite quadrature sensitivity, not a sampling confidence interval. D, Full untruncated diagram bottleneck distances expose severe resolution sensitivity of the high-energy landscape, particularly H1. These large differences prevent a continuum persistence claim even though the low-energy weighted summaries change little. No diagram represents molecular spatial cavities or receptor binding.
